title: M3M India — Risk & Reputation Research
content:
M3M India has received numerous customer complaints and negative reviews highlighting issues with customer service, project maintenance, and management practices. On Trustpilot, a reviewer described M3M India as "fraud people" and detailed a two-year struggle for accountability and communication. Another review on MouthShut criticized the unresponsive customer service and poor maintenance of amenities. On Indeed, multiple reviews from management staff described an unorganized, unprofessional culture with low job security and poor work-life balance. The sources do not provide a definitive answer to the overall satisfaction level of all customers.

Do not buy any property with M3M India Pvt Ltd. They are nothing but fraud people. I have been chasing them since 2 years starting from Nov 2021 after paying them 10% of unit. Sent lots of reminders and called them couple of times. Even visited their office flying out of UK to India but they never could provide me any builder buyer agreement till date. I even discussed it with their Head of sales Anjoo Gogia, head of CRM Deepak and no one could provide me any solution. When I started spreading [...] Day 3: Nothing happened.  
  
Day 5: Still nothing. No communication from my Relationship Manager.  
  
Today: Complete silence. No calls. No replies to my emails.  
  
A company that makes commitments and then completely ignores its customers is unreliable and untrustworthy.  
  
Warning to others: If you are considering buying any unit with m3m Broadyway, be prepared for false promises and a complete lack of accountability when things go wrong. What I found most frustrating, however, was the customer service, or rather, the complete absence of it. Every time I had an issue, whether it was a broken appliance or a problem with the plumbing, reaching someone who could actually help was like pulling teeth. The staff is completely unresponsive, and when you do manage to get a response, it’s often a vague promise that never materializes. I’ve had to chase down service personnel on multiple occasions, and more often than not, they would [...] When it comes to amenities, I found them to be severely lacking. The swimming pool, touted as one of the main selling points of the project, is poorly maintained. It’s often dirty, with debris floating around, and the clubhouse is no better. The gymnasium is small, cramped, and lacks the equipment you’d expect from a luxury development. In fact, everything from the tennis courts to the walking paths feels like a half-baked attempt at luxury. They’ve clearly cut corners here, leaving residents [...] I have unit with M3M Soulitude 2 sector 89 - unit no - M/104/1st floor. First of all they only give me 30 days to pay 90 lakh and when I was not able to pay in 30 days and took around 60 days. They made me to pay interest charges which I paid but now they are telling me - because your unit had intreast charges - all your benefits and null and vide now in case you need to transfer this unit. You need to pay 550 per sqft Transfer charges. Scam scam scam

According to the sources, M3M India has experienced delays in delivery, with an average delay of 8–12 months beyond the originally promised possession date. Specific projects like M3M Soulitude in Gurugram have faced more severe issues, including missed possession timelines by several years, subpar construction quality, and unfulfilled amenity promises. While some projects have delivered on time, others have faced significant delays and quality issues, leading to mixed reviews on communication and post-possession maintenance. The sources do not provide a definitive answer on the overall service quality beyond these specific instances.

At the same time, feedback varies across projects. Some purchasers have reported delays in possession, slower communication during construction, or longer timelines for resolving post-possession issues. Such experiences reinforce the importance of evaluating each project individually rather than relying on brand perception. [...] Like most large developers operating in the NCR region, M3M’s delivery history reflects a combination of completed developments, phased deliveries, and projects that have experienced delays. Delivery timelines in real estate are influenced by regulatory approvals, labour availability, financing conditions, supply chain disruptions, and extraordinary events such as the COVID-19 pandemic. [...] The m3m india delivery record includes numerous completed residential developments as well as projects that have experienced delays due to market conditions, regulatory processes, and external factors. Buyers should verify the latest construction status and possession timelines on the official Haryana RERA (HARERA) portal.

That said, M3M is not the right fit for value-segment or first-time buyers on tight budgets. And possession delays in specific phased projects like M3M Soulitude are a documented concern. We go into both below.

## Delivery & Possession Track Record [...] However, let's not airbrush the record. Buyers at M3M Soulitude (Gurugram) have filed complaints citing possession timelines missed by several years, subpar construction quality in certain phases, and unfulfilled amenity promises. There are also visible complaint proceedings on Haryana RERA involving at least one M3M Urbana Premium matter. These are not isolated grievances — they reflect the friction that large, multi-phase township projects routinely generate. [...] Where buyers get frustrated: post-possession maintenance can be inconsistent, particularly in the early months after handover. Some buyers in multi-phase projects have reported receiving possession in an environment where common areas were still under construction next door — a real quality-of-life concern. Communication from the developer's customer service team during construction gets mixed reviews, with delayed updates cited frequently on buyer forums.

A Delhi court upheld cheating and criminal conspiracy proceedings against M3M India Pvt. Ltd., its promoters, and others in a ₹450-crore land fraud case, directing the trial court to proceed expeditiously. The court set aside the charge of criminal breach of trust under Section 406 IPC, stating that even if every allegation in the FIR is accepted, that offence is not made out. M3M India and its group companies argued that the dispute was purely civil and contractual in nature, but the court rejected these arguments. The company has stated it is ready to pursue every remedy available to them in the court of law and has full faith in the judicial process.

“We have seen reports on the order dated 17 October 2026 passed by the Ld. Principal District and Sessions Judge, Tis Hazari, in the revision petitions filed by M3M India and its group companies. Several of these reports describe the order as a setback for the company. That is not what the order says,” the statement read.

Talking about the remaining allegations, the company said that they are ready to pursue every remedy available to them in the court of law. [...] "M3M has full faith in the judicial process and will continue to cooperate with it," the company said.

Earlier on October 25, it was reported that a Delhi court has declined to interfere with cheating and criminal conspiracy proceedings against M3M India Pvt Ltd, its subsidiary companies and several individuals in a Gurugram land dispute, allowing the criminal case to proceed on allegations that the agreed consideration for a land exchange was not paid. [...] Listen to this article in summarized format

Refuting media reports calling the a ‘setback’, M3M added, “The Court set aside the charge of criminal breach of trust under Section 406 IPC. It held that even if every allegation in the FIR is accepted as it stands, that offence is not made out. This was one of the main allegations MGF Developments made against us.”

A Delhi court has upheld the cheating and criminal conspiracy proceedings against M3M India Pvt. Ltd., its promoters Basant Bansal, Roop Kumar Bansal and Pankaj Bansal, and others in an alleged ₹450-crore land fraud case.

Principal District and Sessions Judge Anju Bajaj Chandna passed the order while hearing revision petitions filed by M3M India Pvt. Ltd., its promoters, challenging the trial court's order taking cognisance of the offences. [...] The case relates to allegations by MGF Developments Ltd.that M3M and its group companies obtained rights over around 31 acres of land in Chauma village in Gurugram without paying the full consideration agreed upon in a land exchange deal.

The court upheld the proceedings for cheating and criminal conspiracy under IPC Sections 420, 120-B and 34 and directed the trial court to proceed expeditiously. The accused have been directed to appear before the Chief Judicial Magistrate on October 27. [...] Challenging the trial court's January 31 order taking cognisance of the offences, the accused argued that MGF had no locus standi to lodge the complaint and that the dispute was purely civil and contractual in nature.

They also contended that the land exchange deeds were executed by separate land-owning companies and that the outstanding amount had subsequently been deposited in court.

- Denial of allegations and assertion that the complaint is liable to be dismissed for selective reliance on the Builder Buyers Agreement (BBA).
- Claim that complainants are not consumers but investors who deliberately avoided taking possession.
- Objection to jurisdiction of the Consumer Commission, asserting the matter is a civil dispute governed by arbitration as per the BBA. [...] The Court examined the factual matrix and contractual terms, finding that the opposite party delayed possession beyond the promised timeline and altered the flat’s layout unilaterally without the complainant’s consent. It rejected the opposite party’s reliance on clauses 13.3 and 13.4 of the Builder Buyers Agreement, holding these to be onerous and unfair terms inconsistent with Supreme Court precedent. The absence of essential amenities such as electricity and water was noted as further [...] - Opposite party's insistence on an Indemnity Bond as a precondition to possession is illegal.
- Claim for refund of the amount paid along with interest at 24%, compensation for interest on housing loan, mental harassment, and litigation costs.
- Opposite party's reliance on clauses permitting changes in plans is contrary to Supreme Court rulings prohibiting unfair trade practices.

M3M India has faced significant reputation problems and criticism, according to the sources. Trustpilot reviews describe M3M as a fraudulent company that fails to provide builder buyer agreements, leaks personal information, sells properties without consent, and refuses to return money. Legal and regulatory scrutiny includes a cheating case and investigations for alleged money laundering. Common complaints include possession delays and specification changes after booking. While M3M's physical structures are reliable, the company's financial transparency is lower than that of publicly traded developers like DLF and Godrej Properties.

### Corporate Legal Battles and Land Deal Disputes

At the macro level, M3M Group has faced highly publicized legal and regulatory scrutiny. A Delhi court took cognisance of a cheating case against M3M and summoned its promoters regarding alleged fraud and breach of trust in a massive land deal with MGF Developments. Furthermore, the company has faced investigations by the Enforcement Directorate regarding alleged money laundering and the attachment of assets worth hundreds of crores. [...] Ultimately, the physical structures they build are highly reliable. The real risk when investing with M3M is falling for the exaggerated promises of unethical brokers in the secondary market and failing to secure your paperwork. The goal of this M3M India review is to ensure you have the raw facts before signing any Builder Buyer Agreement.

## Track the Latest M3M Developments and News [...] For a retail investor, reading that a developer is fighting cheating allegations and ED probes is terrifying. However, the critical takeaway is how these billionaire promoter battles impact actual construction. Historically, M3M has navigated these legal hurdles by substituting attached properties with alternate commercial assets (as permitted by the Supreme Court), ensuring their active project developments proceed without halting. It is a red flag for corporate governance, but it rarely stops

1. Possession delays — The most frequent complaint, affecting approximately 40% of buyers in older M3M projects (source: Haryana RERA complaint database, January–March 2026)
2. Specification changes after booking — Buyers report downgrades from brochure specifications in flooring quality, bathroom fittings, and kitchen hardware [...] M3M's financial transparency is significantly lower than that of listed giants like DLF or Godrej Properties. The company operates with a financial profile similar to other large unlisted Gurugram players like Conscient and Emaar India. [...] For buyers, this means: M3M is very unlikely to disappear mid-construction, but you have less visibility into balance sheet stress than you would with a publicly traded developer. If financial transparency is a top priority, DLF and Godrej Properties offer a more auditable track record.
